author: GUNSjk20
quote: For a game that presents itself as "The most Realistic GTA Ever", the violence is very cartoony. Headshots are just red chunks exploding in 360 directions, no exit wounds, blood spurts from the impact. Have the VFX artists never seen a real gun shot wound??? Story is incredibly boring and I do not at all care for the "Couples Love" gimmick. In a GTA game where you can seemingly do anything and everything, you are very limited to what to do. What if I just want to solo as Jason? NOPE. What if I choose to break up with what's-her-name(I already forgot cause I don't care for her story) but NOPE. This game ties you down so much its practically a Trailing Mission for majority of the game. I really wanted to break up with Lucia(?) and hook up with Jason's ex Mandy cause damn she's the better choice. What kind of woman neglects her child, hides it from Jason, then goes back to doing more crime? A toxic **** Lucia that's who. I'm going back to GTA4. I can't even get a refund cause how the **** are you to refund a digital code.

author: GUNSjk20
quote:
With the gaming industry pushing hard for microtransactions, season passes, forced online, and **** DLC that should've been in game at launch. STRAY is a breath of fresh air. Its a solid well put together game that knows what its doing from start to finish. I wasn't greeted with a Terms and Agreement forms when I booted up STRAY so that's a huge plus. So yeah I'm giving this a 10 cause it was fun to play all the way through and it doesn't push what modern game publishers are doing. I had no performance issues, no bugs or glitches.  Also you play as a Cat with a dedicated Meow button. I'm glad this game didn't follow the “Simulator” genre.

If there is a sequel, I'd like to play as the other Cats trying to find the orange Cat.

Graphics: Quite beautiful, the team really did good with the lighting and shaders.
Controls: Very fluid.
Sounds: Absolutely atmospheric.
Music: 100% gets you immersed in the world.
Story: Its good. It didn't drag on, it showed me what was necessary.

author: GUNSjk20
quote:
In terms of video games, how to be a happy Sonic Fan post Generations.... you can't.

Since the first trailer this game had already many red flags:Over excessive use of bloom, darks are darker, lights are lighter, the assets were ripped from the wii version, Sonic animations in game are broken, and the use of "Tails Saves". And a later trailer showed off the "Ultimate" version next to the Wii version, either SEGA or Blind Squirrel purposefully made the Wii version look like trash to boost people's interest. Non of the issues present in the trailers have been fixed, even worse is that people's saves are being corrupted and for switch users, seizure inducing glitches. Granted the player has to go out of their way to trigger this visual melt downs. Sometimes the Switch version dips under 15fps. Don't know why the team decided to use a new open source Godot engine for this project.  This is supposed to be an ULTIMATE version of a **** Wii game. If you really wanted a better experience for Sonic Colors, play it on Dolphin with 60fps boost. Any modern PC or Phone can run it. SEGA, either put one of your owned studios to work or find a capable company that can deliver on quality. **** hell...
Listen, going off tangent here, I've been a Sonic fan since 1991, we had our ups and hard downs. But I'm exhausted of SEGA or **** Iizuka lying to us fans. If SEGA hadn't released Maina, that would've been it for a majority of fans. Unleashed was a breath of fresh air, Colors stabilized the foundation, and Generations put the building blocks of what a good Sonic game can be.

Graphics: Cataract and Glaucoma simulator
Controls: Sonic is literally slower in this version
Sounds: Too loud
Music: Originals are 100% better
Story: Didn't age well
Added Content: Don't even bother its trash

I paid way to much money for this game, and that's coming from a guy who paid $9 for Forces on launch date.
